elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 2.1: "Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment...", replacing the former USD 2,000,000/year three-year take-or-pay. Reinforced by retained § 12.3 acknowledgement that Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment.

elements.element: Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 2.1: "...and will pay only for Services used or ordered during the applicable term." "Services" is the defined term from § 1.7, so no dangling reference.

elements.element: The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: No commitment survives in the operative text; the redline eliminates rather than limits a commitment. The 12-month limitation appears only in the margin comment as an offered fallback, not in operative language.

elements.element: Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: No reduction-on-notice mechanic appears in rendered § 2.1 or elsewhere; it is only mentioned in the [Playbook] comment.

elements.element: Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: No true-up or shortfall mechanic is drafted; the shortfall/take-or-pay language was deleted entirely rather than converted.

elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
elements.evidence: Cross-level note: the preferred outcome (no commitment at all) is achieved in § 2.1, which exceeds the fallback's purpose, but the fallback checklist itself is unsatisfied because its elements presuppose a retained commitment.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: rendered § 2.1 delivers both preferred elements in one sentence — no minimum purchase or volume commitment, and payment only for Services used or ordered.

The fallback level is not met (no 12-month limitation, no 30-day reduction right, no true-up), but that is immaterial because only one level must be complete, and the redline targets the preferred level.

Minimal: the edit replaces only the offending § 2.1 take-or-pay sentence with a concise substitute; no other paragraph was altered, § 12.3 was retained verbatim, and no extras (survival tails, procedures, damages categories) were added.

Preserves intent: the substituted sentence resolves the pre-existing contradiction with § 12.3's no-minimum-volume acknowledgement, leaves § 7.1's bar on minimum-use charges and § 9.4's convenience right undisturbed, and creates no undefined term or dangling cross-reference ('Services' is defined at § 1.7; 'applicable term' tracks the Order Form/term structure).

The original clause (three-year take-or-pay expressly 'without reduction or termination rights') is squarely walk-away under the rule, so classifying the finding as a deviation and redlining is correct.
